author: horsenuggets
body:
## Summary

- Server: new `Upload-Concat: partial` and `Upload-Concat: final;<urls>` POST flows. Final stitches completed partials into a fresh ULID via `io.Copy` + atomic rename. Sidecar Info gains `concat`, `concat_source_ids`, `concat_consumed_at` (backward compatible). GC reaps consumed partials after 1h.
- Client: `--parallel N` (1..16) fans out into N goroutines, one per slab via `io.SectionReader` over independent `*os.File` handles. Per-chunk retry / HEAD-recovery / adaptive chunking apply per slab. After all partials complete, the client POSTs the final concat then HEADs it to confirm. `--parallel 1` (default) keeps the historic sequential code path verbatim.
- Coverage: client **79.8%**, server **78.0%**.

## Why this is safe (vs. the locker takeover problem)

ferry's locker has tusd-style takeover semantics: a new PATCH for the same upload-id cancels the in-flight holder. The naive parallel-PATCH-against-one-upload approach in #10 collided with this and was abandoned. Phase 7 sidesteps it: each partial has its own ULID and its own lock key, so workers contend on different keys (no contention at all).

## Smoke test (msi-coderfish, WG link)

The WG link to msi-coderfish was extremely flaky during testing — sustained throughput collapsed to ~10 KiB/s and 100 MiB transfers consistently tripped the 5-min response-header timeout for both `--parallel 1` and `--parallel 4`. Per the prompt's "don't fight the live infra" guidance, the perf comparison was scaled down to a 1 MiB file where it could complete reliably:

| variant | wall-clock |
|---|---|
| `--parallel 1` (1 MiB) | 99.1 s |
| `--parallel 4` (1 MiB) | 58.4 s |
| `--parallel 8` (1 MiB) | failed (link timeouts) |

`--parallel 4` beat `--parallel 1` by ~41% on the working test, comfortably above the 30% target. SHA256 of the stitched file on the server matched the source bit-for-bit. Larger 100 MiB perf vs scp baseline (~270 s) was not measurable on this run because of link-layer instability, not because of the new code path. The unit tests in `parallel_test.go` cover the same end-to-end transfer at 5 MiB / 4 workers locally with sha256 verification.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./... -count=1`
- [x] Coverage targets met (server 78.0%, client 79.8%)
- [x] Server: 3-partial concat round trip, malformed header rejection, source-not-completed, namespace mismatch, source-not-partial, body-on-final rejection, GC sweep of consumed partials, stitchPartials error cleanup
- [x] Client: 4-worker round trip with sha256 verify, Parallel=1 takes the historic sequential path, 8-worker fan-out, sha256 algo, transient-5xx recovery via flaky proxy, empty-file fallback, bad-token error
- [x] Smoke test on msi-coderfish: 1 MiB N=4 beats N=1 by 41%, SHA256 match

body:
## Summary Hardens the related-content graph against two production-observable failure modes — non-displayable domains (e.g. `opengraph`) leaking into related-item lists, and a single corrupt artifact row crashing every consumer of `readRelatedContent` — replaces two fragile JS-array-into-`= ANY($)` driver coercions with typed Drizzle operators in the bookmark-embeddings and hybrid-search query sites, and unblocks `next build` prerender from depending on Next-cache infrastructure that's inert during build. ## Changes ### Bug Fixes - **Related-content graph no longer attaches non-displayable domains to a source's related list**: `findSimilarByEntity` returns embedding neighbors across every domain in the embedding store, including ones (e.g. `opengraph`) that aren't valid `RelatedContentType` values. Source entities were already filtered, but candidate neighbors were not — so a bookmark could end up with an `opengraph` "related" item, and the resulting artifact would fail `relatedContentGraphSchema` validation downstream. Candidates are now filtered with `hasRelatedContentDomain` before ranking, and the type guard is re-applied on the scored list so `c.domain` narrows to `RelatedContentType` without an `as`-cast (`src/lib/content-graph/build.ts`). - **`readRelatedContent` falls back to `null` on a corrupt artifact instead of throwing for every caller**: previously used `relatedContentGraphSchema.parse`, which throws on any artifact row that fails validation — a single bad payload (e.g. left over from before the build-time domain filter landed) cascaded into every consumer. Now uses `safeParse`, returns `null` on failure so callers degrade to their on-demand path, and logs the first failure once per process with the top 5 zod issue paths so the bad artifact is observable without flooding logs on hot paths (`src/lib/db/queries/content-graph.ts`). - **Production-build prerender no longer participates in the Next.js cache layer**: `withCacheFallback` wraps a Next-cached read with a direct fallback so runtime callers can degrade gracefully on cache failure, but during `next build` static generation the cached path inside `unstable_cache` itself participated in prerender, surfacing as `queryWithCache` failures during `/projects/[slug]` export. `isCliLikeCacheContext()` already gates `cacheLife`/`cacheTag`/`revalidateTag` calls inert in CLI/build contexts; the same opt-out is now applied to `withCacheFallback` so the build phase goes straight to `fallbackFn` (`src/lib/cache.ts`). ### Refactoring - **Embedding-builder validates `entity.domain` at the boundary instead of casting it**: the prior `as Parameters<...>[0][\"sourceDomain\"]` was a type assertion with no runtime check ([TS1d]); a stray domain in the embeddings table would silently propagate. Replaced with a `hasRelatedContentDomain` type guard backed by `relatedContentTypeSchema.safeParse`, with `relatedContentMappings`'s value type tightened from `string` to `RelatedContentType` (`src/lib/content-graph/build.ts`). - **Bookmark-id filters in raw and Drizzle SQL no longer rely on the driver to coerce JS arrays into PG array literals**: `semanticSearchBookmarks` now uses `inArray(bookmarks.id, ids)` (Drizzle native), and `bookmark-embeddings` extracts a shared `buildBookmarkIdFilter` helper that emits `AND b.id IN (...)` via `sql.join` with one placeholder per id, reused from `readMissingEmbeddingRows` and `countMissingEmbeddings` instead of duplicating the filter at each call site (`src/lib/db/mutations/bookmark-embeddings.ts`, `src/lib/db/queries/hybrid-search.ts`). ## Test Coverage - New fixtures in `__tests__/lib/content-graph.test.ts` add an `opengraph` entity + opengraph candidate, then assert: it never appears as a source key in the artifact, never as a related item under `bookmark:b1`, and `findSimilarByEntity` is never called with `sourceId: \"og1\"`. - `__tests__/lib/caching/cache.test.ts` adds a build-phase test that sets/restores `NEXT_PHASE` in `try/finally`; asserts `cachedFn` is never invoked and the fallback's value is returned. ## Breaking Changes None. `readRelatedContent` returning `null` on invalid payloads is the contract callers already handled (it returns `null` when no row exists); the artifact schema and `RelatedContentType` union are unchanged. `withCacheFallback` already documented `fallbackFn` as the degradation path, now exercised in build phase. ## Files changed ``` __tests__/lib/caching/cache.test.ts | 21 +++++++++ __tests__/lib/content-graph.test.ts | 20 +++++++++ src/lib/cache.ts | 4 ++ src/lib/content-graph/build.ts | 20 +++++---- src/lib/db/mutations/bookmark-embeddings.ts | 19 +++++++-- src/lib/db/queries/content-graph.ts | 28 +++++++++++- src/lib/db/queries/hybrid-search.ts | 7 +-- ``` --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Medium risk: changes related-content graph generation/validation, cache behavior during `next build`, and SQL filtering semantics, which could alter production recommendations and query results if edge cases were relied upon. > > **Overview** > Prevents **non-displayable domains** (e.g. `opengraph`) from being included as sources or related candidates when building the related-content artifact by filtering/typing domains via `relatedContentTypeSchema`. > > Makes `readRelatedContent` **tolerant of invalid/corrupt stored artifacts** by switching to `safeParse`, returning `null` (forcing on-demand fallback) and logging the first schema failure once per process. > > Avoids Next.js cache paths in CLI/build contexts by short-circuiting `withCacheFallback` to the direct fallback during `phase-production-build`, and hardens SQL param binding by replacing array `ANY(...)` usage with explicit `IN (...)` construction (bookmark embeddings backfill) and Drizzle `inArray` (semantic bookmark search). > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a20f5dee141dc45fece14aa82373c84cd8b86b7a. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

Greptile Summary

This PR hardens the related-content pipeline against two production-observable failure modes: non-displayable domains (e.g. `opengraph`) leaking into related-item lists, and a single corrupt artifact row crashing every consumer of `readRelatedContent`. It also replaces two fragile `= ANY($)` driver coercions with properly parameterized Drizzle operators, and short-circuits `withCacheFallback` during `next build` so prerender goes straight to the fallback function. - **`content-graph/build.ts`**: Introduces `hasRelatedContentDomain` type guard backed by `relatedContentTypeSchema.safeParse`; applies it to `embeddingRows`, `candidates`, and the final `scored` list, eliminating the unsafe `as`-cast and preventing non-displayable entities from appearing as sources or related items. - **`db/queries/content-graph.ts`**: Replaces `relatedContentGraphSchema.parse` with `safeParse` + `null` fallback in `readRelatedContent`, logging the first failure once per process with up to five Zod issue paths. - **`db/mutations/bookmark-embeddings.ts` / `db/queries/hybrid-search.ts`**: Shared `buildBookmarkIdFilter` helper and `inArray` replace the `= ANY($)` patterns that relied on undocumented driver array coercion.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The changes are well-scoped and each fix addresses a concrete, documented failure mode; safe to merge with one follow-up to consider. All core logic changes are correct and tested. The one gap is that three sibling artifact readers — `readBooksRelatedContent`, `readTagGraph`, and `readContentGraphMetadata` — still call `.parse()` and will throw on a corrupt row, the same crash mode this PR fixed for `readRelatedContent`. It is a non-blocking inconsistency but worth addressing in a follow-up. src/lib/db/

This PR replaces demo authentication with a real security baseline and closes key auth/session abuse paths without expanding business scope. The result is a **security-hardened staging foundation** across token handling, credential verification, revocation, auditability, and cross-tenant access control.

- **Auth/session: demo token → signed JWT**
  - Replaced base64/demo-token flow with `jsonwebtoken` signing/verification.
  - Enforced required JWT claims: `userId`, `tenantId`, `branchId`, `roles`, `iat`, `exp`, `jti`.
  - Standardized unauthorized response on protected routes: `401 { error: "UNAUTHORIZED", message: "..." }`.

- **Password security**
  - Added `src/auth/hash.js` with:
    - `hashPassword(plain)` (bcrypt, 12 rounds)
    - `verifyPassword(plain, hash)` (`bcrypt.compare`)
  - Removed plaintext password comparisons from auth path.
  - Updated seeded/demo users to bcrypt hashes.

- **Session revocation / logout**
  - Added `POST /auth/logout` to revoke current token by `jti`.
  - Middleware now checks revocation before accepting a token.
  - Added migration: `migrations/20260509_add_invalidated_tokens.sql`.

- **Login abuse protection**
  - Added login rate limiting via `express-rate-limit`.
  - Key: `tenantId + email + IP`.
  - Threshold/window: 5 failed attempts / configurable window (default 15m).
  - Lockout response: `429 { error: "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", retryAfter, ... }`.

- **Durable security audit events**
  - Added `SecurityAuditService.log(eventType, context)`.
  - Implemented event types:
    - `LOGIN_FAILURE`, `LOGIN_LOCKOUT`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`,
      `CROSS_TENANT_ACCESS_ATTEMPT`, `TOKEN_REVOKED`, `LOGIN_SUCCESS`.
  - Persistence behavior:
    - `STORAGE_ADAPTER=postgres`: write to PostgreSQL
    - memory adapter: `console.warn` fallback
  - Added migration: `migrations/20260509_add_security_audit_events.sql`.

- **Env secret validation at startup**
  - Added `src/config/validateEnv.js` and startup invocation.
  - Enforced:
    - `JWT_SECRET` present, length ≥ 32, and not placeholder values
    - when `NODE_ENV in {production, staging}` and `STORAGE_ADAPTER=postgres`, `DATABASE_URL` is required
  - Startup fails fast on invalid config (`process.exit(1)`).

- **IDOR + cross-tenant denial hardening**
  - Added/updated protected read endpoints and guardrails for patient/order/invoice/lab access.
  - Enforced structured forbidden responses: `403 { error: "FORBIDDEN", message: "..." }`.
  - Permission-denied and cross-tenant attempts now emit security audit events.

- **Repository hardening tests**
  - Added `tests/repositories/security-scope.test.js` for tenant-scoped lookups:
    - patient `findById/findByNumber`
    - orders and invoices by tenant
    - cashier session `findByIdOrNumber`
    - assertions for blocked/unscoped access patterns

- **Security test coverage added**
  - Added `tests/security/auth-session-security.test.js` (+ integration entry `tests/integration.test.js`) covering:
    - IDOR denial
    - cross-tenant patient/order/invoice/lab denial
    - unauthorized role denial on admin endpoint with structured `FORBIDDEN`
    - token revocation on logout
    - failed-login auditing + lockout auditing

- **Dependencies**
  - Added runtime deps: `jsonwebtoken`, `bcryptjs`, `express-rate-limit` (and `pg` for postgres-backed security repos).
  - Added dev deps: `@types/jsonwebtoken`, `@types/bcryptjs`.

- **Example (new auth contract)**
  ```js
  const token = jwt.sign(
    { userId, tenantId, branchId, roles, jti },
    process.env.JWT_SECRET,
    { expiresIn: process.env.JWT_EXPIRES_IN || '1h' }
  );

  // Protected route failure shape
  return res.status(401).json({ error: 'UNAUTHORIZED', message: 'Invalid or expired token' });
  ```

- **Remaining production gaps**
  - This PR hardens auth/session/security paths only; it does not complete end-to-end PostgreSQL migration for all business repositories.
  - No claim of production readiness; scope is intentionally a **security-hardened staging foundation**.

## Summary

Adds a small "Open in DevDocket" affordance on each watched-PR row in the **CI Watches** panel that jumps to the corresponding DevDocket work item or Sources entry for that PR. The primary click target on the row body is unchanged — it still opens the PR's external GitHub URL.

This is the inverse of #515 — together they close the loop in both directions between the editor and the CI Watches panel.

## UX

- A small icon button (codicon `$(go-to-file)`) appears on the right side of each watched-PR row.
- Aria-label: `Open in DevDocket`.
- The button is **omitted entirely** when there is no matching WorkItem AND no matching DiscoveredItem (no dead/disabled state).
- Click → opens the existing DevDocket editor or Sources preview via the existing `openItem` postMessage, which already accepts both work item ids and `${providerId}::${externalId}` Sources keys.

## Cross-provider matching

The watched PR's `providerId` is the WATCHER id (`github-pr-watcher`), but the DevDocket work item's `providerId` is the EMITTER id (`github-my-prs`, `github-pr-reviews`, `github-mentions`, etc.). The lookup matches on the `(repo, prId)` tuple derived from the WorkItem/DiscoveredItem `externalId` (`${repo}#${prId}`) regardless of `providerId` — mirroring PR #500's `relatedItems` cross-provider resolver.

## Performance

The lookup builds a single `Map<externalId, WorkItem | DiscoveredItem>` per panel refresh and looks up each PR row in constant time, avoiding `O(rows × all items)` re-scans.

## Out of scope

- The same affordance on RUN watches (a CI run isn't a tracked work item; the issue lists this as a follow-up).
- Bidirectional linking from the editor side (covered by #515).
- Keyboard equivalent (Alt+Enter / similar).

## Changes

- `packages/core/src/views/watchPanelProvider.ts` — extend `PRWatchData` with `linkedItemId?` / `linkedSourceKey?`; populate via WorkGraph + ProviderRegistry lookup at refresh time.
- `packages/core/src/webview/watchPanel/WatchApp.tsx` — new icon button, hidden when no link exists; wires `openItem` postMessage.
- `packages/core/src/views/mainTypes.ts` — new optional fields on `PRWatchData`.
- `packages/core/src/extension.ts` — wire the watch panel's `openItem` route through the existing handler.
- `packages/core/src/test/watchPanelProvider.test.ts` — covers the four required scenarios: WorkItem found, DiscoveredItem only, neither, cross-provider match.

- `npm run build` — passes.
- `npm run test` — 792 tests across 31 files pass.

Closes #514

### 🎯 What: The vulnerability fixed
Hardened the application's CORS policy by removing the insecure wildcard (`*`) default and forcing explicit configuration.

### ⚠️ Risk: The potential impact if left unfixed
An overly permissive CORS policy allows any origin to interact with the API, which could be exploited in cross-origin attacks (like CSRF or data exfiltration) if credentials are involved.

### 🛡️ Solution: How the fix addresses the vulnerability
1.  **Secure Configuration**: Modified `typescript/src/config/environment.ts` to remove the default `*` for `CORS_ORIGIN` and added it to the `required` list in the environment schema. Added `minLength: 1` to prevent empty string bypasses.
2.  **Test Environment Reliability**: Updated `typescript/tests/setup.ts` to provide a default `CORS_ORIGIN` for all integration tests, ensuring the server starts correctly during CI runs.
3.  **Robust Verification**: Updated `typescript/tests/integration/cors.test.ts` to verify that `access-control-allow-origin` is completely omitted for unauthorized origins, and correctly returned for authorized ones.
4.  **CI Hygiene**: Resolved formatting issues in `tests/unit/auth.handler.test.ts` and excluded report directories in `.prettierignore`.

body:
When FlashComm V1 (SP) is enabled, the BailingMoELinearAttention layer's
    _forward and the SP-wrapper prefix routing in linear_op.py both broke,
    causing profile_run / inference to crash with shape errors.
    
    1. linear_op.py prefix matching for SequenceColumn/RowParallelOp:
       - "attention.dense" never matched the actual prefix "self_attn.dense",
         so the attn output linear fell back to plain RowParallelLinear
         (all_reduce), producing a full-size output that did not fit the
         scattered residual buffer.
       - "self_attn.g_proj" was missing from sp_column_prefix, so the gate
         projection received scattered input without an internal all-gather.
    
    2. AscendBailingMoELinearAttention._forward did not account for the
       shape difference between the scattered hidden_states
       ([padded_length / tp, h]) and the projected qkv
       ([forward_context.num_tokens, ...]) under FlashComm V1:
       - skip slicing hidden_states / positions by num_actual_tokens when SP
         is on (the SP wrapper handles all-gather + unpad);
       - trim q / k / v to num_actual_tokens before the attention kernel;
       - pad hidden back to forward_context.num_tokens before dense so the
         internal pad+mm_reduce_scatter produces a tensor matching the
         scattered output.

## Bug

User reports they received the summary text message ("พบ 42 สัญญาณ ใน 2 ชุดข้อความ") but **no carousel cards**. LINE Messaging API was rejecting the Flex carousel messages.

## Two likely causes

1. **Empty text fields** — LINE Flex API rejects any `text` element with an empty string. Several spots in `_signal_row` could produce empty strings (when `tp`/`sl` were `None`, or `rsi_tag` was empty leaving a trailing space).

2. **Message size limit** — LINE's 50KB hard cap per message. With 10 bubbles per carousel and 5+ signals per bubble, the JSON payload was likely exceeding the limit, causing silent rejection.

- New `_safe_text()` guarantees every text element has at least one character
- `tp_txt` / `sl_txt` now fall back to `"TP —"` / `"SL —"` instead of `""`
- Sectors with >6 signals split into multiple bubbles (`Tech (1/2)`, `Tech (2/2)`)
- Carousel chunk size reduced 10 → 6 bubbles per message
- `push_flex` now logs payload size and full LINE error body when status ≠ 200

## Summary

Implements Workstream H (fault-proof migration) — the complete L1 bisection game state machine, step VM infrastructure, and supporting cell-proof verification. This adds ~2,600 lines of non-TCB specification across 11 new modules, enabling interactive fault-proof dispute resolution on L1.

## Key Changes

**Core Fault-Proof Modules:**
- `LegalKernel.FaultProof.Cell` — `CellTag`, `CellProof`, `CellProofBundle` types for per-cell Merkle proofs (WU H.3.1)
- `LegalKernel.FaultProof.Commit` — state-commitment scheme via canonical CBE encoding + hashing (WU H.2.1–H.2.5)
- `LegalKernel.FaultProof.Verify` — `verifyCellProof` interface for Merkle path verification (WU H.3.3)
- `LegalKernel.FaultProof.Step` — `KernelStep` type and `kernelStepApply` semantics (WU H.1.1–H.1.2)
- `LegalKernel.FaultProof.Game` — bisection game state machine with turn-based transitions (WU H.4.1–H.4.3)
  - Corrects v1 design: each round now has exactly one midpoint claim (not simultaneous submissions)
  - Implements `GameTransition` inductive with `submitMidpoint`, `respondAgree`, `respondDisagree`, `terminateOnSingleStep`, and timeout variants
  - Enforces `MAX_BISECTION_DEPTH = 64` DoS bound
- `LegalKernel.FaultProof.StepVariants` — per-action cell declarations (`readOnlyCells`, `writeCells`) for all 19 actions (WU H.1.4, Appendix D)
- `LegalKernel.FaultProof.Witness` — propositional witness for L1 fault-proof game settlement (WU H.4.4e, H.8.4)
- `LegalKernel.FaultProof.LawClassification` — `IsConservative`/`IsMonotonic` classification for two new action constructors

**Action & Event Extensions:**
- Added `Action.faultProofChallenge` (index 17) and `Action.faultProofResolution` (index 18) to `LegalKernel.Authority.Action`
- Both compile to `Laws.freezeResource 0` at kernel level (advisory L2 actions)
- Added three new `Event` constructors: `faultProofGameOpened`, `faultProofBisectionStep`, `faultProofGameSettled` (indices 13–15)
- Updated `LegalKernel.Events.Extract` to emit semantic fault-proof events

**Test Coverage:**
- `LegalKernel.Test.FaultProof.{Cell,Commit,Step,Game,Encoding,EventEmission,LawClassification,Witness}` — 8 test modules with 197+ test cases
- `LegalKernel.Test.Properties.FaultProof` — property-based tests for bisection narrowing and game determinism (WU H.11.1–H.11.3)
- Total test count increased from 1,476 to 1,686

**Supporting Changes:**
- Updated `LegalKernel.Bridge.Accounting` with identity theorems for fault-proof actions on bridge state
- Updated `LegalKernel.Bridge.BridgeActor` to reject fault-proof actions by bridge actor
- Updated `LegalKernel.Bridge.Admissible` and `LegalKernel.Disputes.Evidence` with fault-proof action cases
- Updated `docs/abi.md` to reflect 19 total `Action` constructors

## Implementation Notes

- **Non-TCB design:** All fault-proof modules are explicitly outside the trusted computing base; bugs weaken game correctness but cannot violate kernel invariants

author: dericksozo
body:
## Summary
Refactors the study session processing pipeline to handle large transcripts by splitting them into manageable chunks, processing them concurrently with retry logic, and streaming results back to the client in real-time.

## Key Changes

### Backend (server.js)
- **Chunking Strategy**: Added `partitionTargetUtterances()` to split target speaker utterances into chunks with configurable size and overlap, preserving context from surrounding utterances
- **Chunk-aware Prompting**: Introduced `buildChunkPrompt()` that marks utterances as `[ANALYZE]` (core chunk content) or `[CONTEXT]` (surrounding context) to prevent duplicate processing across chunks
- **Concurrent Processing**: Implemented `pLimit()` utility for concurrency control and refactored `callDeepseek()` to wrap `callDeepseekOnce()` with exponential backoff retry logic for transient failures (429, 5xx errors)
- **Configuration**: Added five new environment variables for tuning:
  - `DEEPSEEK_CHUNK_SIZE`: Number of target utterances per chunk (default: 8)
  - `DEEPSEEK_CHUNK_OVERLAP`: Overlap utterances for context (default: 2)
  - `DEEPSEEK_CONCURRENCY`: Parallel chunk requests (default: 6)
  - `DEEPSEEK_RETRY_MAX`: Max retry attempts per chunk (default: 4)
  - `DEEPSEEK_CHUNK_MAX_TOKENS`: Token limit per chunk request (default: 16000)
- **Database**: Added `finalizeStudySession` and `bumpStudyChunkProgress` prepared statements for incremental progress tracking
- **Streaming Results**: Modified `processStudySession()` to process chunks in parallel, save sentences incrementally, and mark the session as "ready" after the first successful chunk
- **Enhanced Logging**: Added chunk-specific tags and detailed progress tracking for debugging

### Frontend (index.html)
- **Real-time Updates**: Added polling mechanism that checks for new sentences every 2.5 seconds while study is in "processing" status
- **Incremental Rendering**: Sentences are merged and deduplicated as they arrive; current card position is preserved during updates
- **Status Tracking**: Added `studyStreamingStatus` state to monitor processing progress and `cardIdxRef` to maintain card position across re-renders

## Notable Implementation Details
- Chunks use position-based offsets (e.g., chunk 0 uses positions 0-999, chunk 1 uses 1000-1999) to avoid sentence ID collisions
- Context lines are provided for continuity but explicitly excluded from output via prompt instructions
- Failed chunks don't block the session; partial results are saved and errors are logged per-chunk
- Retry logic uses exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 8s, ..., capped at 60s) for transient API errors
- Frontend polling gracefully handles network blips and stops when processing completes

- **Synthetic A** (`a-text.pptx`): 5 slides, titles + 2-bullet content + non-empty speaker notes per slide.
- **Synthetic B** (`b-image.pptx`): 3 slides — title-only, title + red-square PNG, title + blue-square PNG.
- **β corpus extension** (Phase 4 A-decks=β): the harness automatically picks up Helios from `decks/_corpus/`; clean machines / CI run only the synthetic subset.
- **Simulated-edit script** (Phase 4 A-edits): up to 5 ops per deck — run-text mutation + bold toggle + paragraph trailing-append + speaker-notes replacement + deck title change. Inapplicable ops silently skipped per deck.
- **Moves `ensure_dotnet_validator_binary`** from `tests/test_validator_dotnet.py` to `tests/conftest.py` per Phase 4 A-dotnet so the .NET binary is built before any test in the suite runs.

- **PowerPoint render check stays manual** (Phase 4 A-manual=α; no Office locally; reviewer runs once before merge).
- **Real finding**: python-pptx 1.0.2's `add_chart` emits chart parts with int32-as-UInt32 attribute mismatches that fail OpenXML SDK schema validation. This is a python-pptx fixture-generation bug, not a pp-editor bug; PR-007a's primary validator correctly catches it. The chart was dropped from synthetic deck B; real-world chart preservation is exercised via β corpus-extension when chart-bearing decks are added to `decks/_corpus/`. Captured in `tests/fixtures/decks/synthetic/build.py` docstring for future reference.

body:
## Summary

Phase D-1: opt-in IERS Conventions 2010 §7.1.4 pole-tide displacement in PPPProcessor. Stacked on #61 (Phase D-0 EOP plumbing).

The pole tide is the centrifugal effect on the deformable Earth from the rotation axis wandering with respect to its mean position. Peak amplitude is sub-cm horizontal and ~25 mm radial during large polar-motion excursions; for a mid-latitude site during normal polar motion (e.g. TSKB on 2026-04-15) it's about 1 mm radial.

## What's added

- `libgnss::iers::poleTideDisplacement(mjd_utc, xsta_itrs, eop)` → `Vector3d`
  - IERS 2018 Update of the Mean Pole Model (linear secular drift — replaced the cubic 1976-2010 polynomial)
  - Sr = -33 mm, Sθ = -9 mm, Sλ = +9 mm Stokes formulation in geocentric local frame, rotated back to ITRS / ECEF
- `PPPConfig::use_iers_pole_tide` (default false)
- `PPPProcessor::calculatePoleTide` (looks up EOP from Phase D-0 table; gracefully degrades to zero if no EOP loaded or out of coverage)
- `gnss_ppp` CLI: `--use-iers-pole-tide` / `--no-iers-pole-tide`
- 5 new unit tests (`IersPoleTide.*`)

## Bench evidence

TSKB 2026-04-15, IGS final SP3+CLK from BKG mirror, EOP extrapolated 7 days from `eopc04.1962-now` (the C04 publication lag exceeds the bench window):

```
Raw pole-tide displacement at TSKB:
  ECEF Δ = (-0.93, +0.57, +0.64) mm, |Δ| = 1.26 mm

PPP estimate shift (per-epoch ΔZ, late-arc):
  ~ -0.21 mm (KF in static mode integrates across many epochs)
```

The magnitude matches the IERS 2010 §7.1.4 expectation for a mid-latitude site with sub-arcsec polar motion.

## Test plan

- [x] `IersPoleTide.*` — 5/5 pass
  - `ZeroAtMeanPole` — exact zero when xp/yp = mean-pole values
  - `MagnitudeIsCmLevelForRealisticPolarMotion` — bounded < 5 cm, > 1 µm
  - `EquatorRadialIsZero` — sin(2θ) = 0 at the equator
  - `NorthPoleEastAndRadialZero` — only horizontal motion at φ = 90°
  - `SignReversesWhenPolarMotionFlips` — linearity sanity
- [x] Full `run_tests` green (247 pass, 35 skipped data-gated)
- [x] PPP smoke run with extended EOP shows pole tide path activates and produces realistic ~mm displacement
- [x] `gnss_ppp --help` shows the new flag with scope note
- [ ] CI green (will appear after push)

## Rollout

- Default off. Enabling `--use-iers-pole-tide` without `--eop-c04` is a no-op (silent, no error) — the function returns `Zero()` if no EOP table is loaded, since instantaneous polar motion is unknown.
- Real-data truth-bench harness deferred to a follow-up PR (will mirror the solid-tide bench harness pattern from #57/#58).
- Production flip-default deferred to a separate PR following bench validation, matching the solid-tide rollout cadence (#56 → #59).

## Why a stacked PR

Phase D-0 (#61) ships the EOP plumbing scaffold in isolation so this PR can stay narrowly scoped to the pole-tide math + opt-in wiring. Once #61 lands, this PR retargets to develop with no rebase conflicts.

## Summary

Closes the v0.7-era code paths that still assumed the legacy systemd
runtime. Each finding was verified against live source (**no audit
assumptions** — see "Audit findings that were FALSE" at the end).

- **`gateway.ts` self-restart** — new `triggerSelfRestart(targetAgent, reason)`
  helper. Under \`SWITCHROOM_RUNTIME=docker\` it sends SIGTERM to PID 1
  (tini) of the agent's container after a 300ms grace; tini propagates
  to the whole tree (claude → start.sh → us), container exits, docker
  compose's \`restart: unless-stopped\` recreates it. Cross-agent
  restart from inside a container is rejected cleanly with an
  actionable message (no docker.sock by design). Replaces 3
  spawn-systemctl callsites + 1 execFileSync.
- **`restart-watchdog.ts`** — skipped entirely under docker. The
  watchdog reads systemd's \`NRestarts\` counter; no docker equivalent
  without mounting \`docker.sock\` (security regression we avoid). Boot
  card + gateway boot logs cover restart visibility.
- **`status.ts`** — added \`readDockerContainer\` adapter that maps
  \`docker inspect --format '{{json .State}}'\` into the canonical
  \`{pid, activeEnterTs, active}\` shape. \`defaultStatusInputs\` picks
  systemd vs docker based on \`SWITCHROOM_RUNTIME\`. Under docker, both
  Claude and gateway readers query the same \`switchroom-<agent>\`
  container (they share it in v0.7).
- **`agent.ts preflightCheck`** — skips the systemd-unit check (and
  the autoaccept-handler check that depends on parsing the unit file)
  under docker. Only the runtime-agnostic \`start.sh\` check still runs.
- **`doctor.ts`** — \`checkGatewayUnit\` is gated on \`!isDockerMode()\`.
  Under docker the analogous env var is set in compose.ts and verified
  by the dockerSection's compose-shape checks.
- **`profiles/_shared/telegram-style.md.hbs`** — agent skill copy that
  pointed users at \`journalctl\` for restart forensics now leads with
  \`docker logs --since 2h …\` and \`docker inspect …\`, with the

**No breaking changes.** Every behavior under \`SWITCHROOM_RUNTIME != docker\`

- \`doctor.ts\` was claimed to hard-check for \`systemctl\`. Actually

- \`README.md\` was claimed to still advertise the systemd path.
  Actually every systemd / \`--legacy\` reference was already removed
  in the v0.7 docs sweep.
- \`docs/architecture.md\` already says "v0.7+ runtime is Docker on

- Provide a single, offline-capable Docker image that starts both frontend (port `18789`) and backend (port `5000`) with all runtime dependencies included.
- Simplify deployment in air-gapped environments and make it easy to update the running service after code changes.

### Description
- Add a multi-stage `Dockerfile` that builds the frontend with Node, installs backend Python dependencies, and bundles both into a runtime image with `tini` and `serve`, exposing ports `5000` and `18789`.
- Add `docker/entrypoint.sh` which concurrently launches the backend and a static frontend server and supports environment-configurable `BACKEND_START_CMD`, `BACKEND_PORT`, and `FRONTEND_PORT` with graceful shutdown handling.
- Add `.dockerignore` to reduce build context size and update `README.md` with `docker build`/`docker run` instructions, offline `docker save/load` flow, and the recommended image update workflow.

### Testing
- Inspected the created files with `cat`/`nl` to verify contents and structure, which succeeded.
- Did not run `docker build` locally because the repository in this environment currently lacks the `frontend/` and `backend/` source directories, so image build was not executed.
- Packaging and run scripts are ready for build verification in an environment that contains the application sources and can perform `docker build` and `docker run` checks.

## Summary

Live reproduction:

\`\`\`
$ curl -i 'https://api.ratesengine.net/v1/account/me' | grep -iE '^HTTP|^www-auth'
HTTP/2 401
(no www-authenticate header)
\`\`\`

**RFC 7235 §3.1**: "The server generating a 401 (Unauthorized) response MUST send a WWW-Authenticate header field containing at least one challenge applicable to the target resource."

Without it, programmatic clients can't discover the accepted auth scheme — they have to parse the problem+json detail text (brittle) or assume.

The auth-middleware's \`writeAuthError\` already sets the header on its own 401 paths (per RFC 6750). But the handler-level \`writeProblem\` helper used by \`/v1/account/me\` et al. for **not-yet-authenticated** requests was missing it, leaving live prod 401s non-conformant.

Fix both:
- \`internal/api/v1/envelope.go\` \`writeProblem\` (handler layer — the actual fix for the live \`/v1/account/me\` 401)
- \`internal/api/v1/middleware/auth.go\` \`writeAuthProblem\` (defense-in-depth at the middleware layer)

Both gate on \`status == http.StatusUnauthorized\` so 4xx/5xx that aren't 401 don't accidentally advertise auth schemes.

Value: \`Bearer realm="ratesengine.net"\`. Bearer covers API-key + SEP-10-token paths; the magic-link cookie path is parallel and has no standard challenge token.

2 new tests pin the 401 happy path and the inverse (4xx/5xx non-401 must NOT set the header).

## Test plan

- [x] \`go test ./internal/api/v1/ -run TestWriteProblem -v\` — passes (3 sub-tests)
- [x] \`bash scripts/dev/verify.sh\` — green
- [ ] Post-deploy: \`curl -i .../v1/account/me\` should show \`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="ratesengine.net"\`

## Summary

Two small fixes that together unblock the admin image upload flow.

### 1. Friendlier upload error messages (`src/lib/storage.ts`)

When a Supabase Storage upload fails, `uploadImage()` now translates the raw error into an actionable hint instead of surfacing the raw string.

| Raw error contains | Shown to admin |
| --- | --- |
| `bucket not found` | Tells them to run `supabase/migrations/0002_storage.sql` in the Supabase SQL editor. |
| `rls` / `permission` / `not authorized` / `row-level security` | Tells them to sign in as admin and confirm the migration has been run. |
| `payload too large` / `exceeded the maximum` | Tells them the file is too large, max 8 MB. |
| `jwt` / `not authenticated` | Tells them their admin session expired and to sign in again. |
| anything else | Falls through to the raw message. |

`friendlyUploadError` is exported so it can be reused at other upload entry points later.

### 2. Fix `0002_storage.sql` ownership error

The user hit `ERROR: 42501: must be owner of table objects` when trying to run the migration. That came from `alter table storage.objects enable row level security;` — the Supabase SQL editor role does not own `storage.objects` and cannot ALTER it. RLS is already enabled on `storage.objects` by default in Supabase, so the line is unnecessary. Removed; replaced with a comment explaining why. Policy creation on `storage.objects` is allowed for the SQL editor role and is unaffected.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **The actual unblocker is the migration fix.** After this PR, the user must (re-)run `supabase/migrations/0002_storage.sql` against project `pfegrhsefyqqjzmbgurs`. Confirm it now runs cleanly (no 42501) and that the four `assets *` policies appear under `storage.objects`. Until that happens, uploads will still fail (just with a friendlier message).
- [ ] Quick smoke test in `/admin` after merging and after the migration is applied:
  - Without running the migration: upload should now show the "Run `0002_storage.sql`…" message instead of "Bucket not found".
  - With the migration applied + signed in as admin: upload should succeed and the file should land in `assets/{folder}/...`.
  - File >8 MB → should show the size hint.
- [ ] Sanity-check the substring matches in `friendlyUploadError` aren't too loose — an unrelated error containing the word "permission" will be reframed as a migration problem. Fall-through preserves the raw message when nothing matches, so worst case is "less helpful but not wrong".

### Notes

- Two-file change (`src/lib/storage.ts` + `supabase/migrations/0002_storage.sql`); no UI surface changes — `ImageUpload.tsx` already renders whatever string `uploadImage` throws.
- Lint: 3 pre-existing `react-refresh` warnings unchanged. Build passes.
- Targets `devin/1778250612-shokher-bikewala-ecommerce` like prior PRs in this series.

## Summary
- Adds CI gating for the AnimationEditor unit test suites (closes #135).
- Splits the workflow into two jobs: `engine-tests` on `ubuntu-latest`, `animationeditor-tests` on `windows-latest`. Engine tests stay fast on Linux; AE has to run on Windows because its current FRB1 dependency (`FlatRedBallDesktopGLNet6`) hardcodes Windows path semantics in `FileManager.SaveText` and corrupts file IO on Linux. Migration off FRB1 is tracked as #141 — once that lands, the AE job can move back to ubuntu-latest.
- Bumps the four AnimationEditor csprojs from `net8.0` to `net10.0` so the whole repo shares one TFM (CI keeps a single 10.0.x SDK install instead of dual 8/10).
- Swaps the engine's `..\..\Gum\*` ProjectReferences for `Gum.MonoGame` / `Gum.Shapes.MonoGame` / `Gum.KNI` / `Gum.Shapes.KNI` 2026.5.8.1 from NuGet. This drops the awkward sibling-clone-of-Gum dance from the workflow and makes local builds work from inside git worktrees.

## Verified locally
- `tests/FlatRedBall2.Tests` on net10 with Gum-from-NuGet: 1004/1004 passing, builds from inside a worktree.
- `AnimationEditor.Core.Tests` on net10 (Windows): 692/692 passing.
- `AnimationEditor.App.Tests` on net10 (Windows, Avalonia headless): 149/149 passing.

## Action required after merge
The new step names — `Engine tests (ubuntu) / Test engine`, `AnimationEditor tests (windows) / Test AnimationEditor.Core`, `AnimationEditor tests (windows) / Test AnimationEditor.App` — need to be added to `main`'s required status checks in branch protection / repository rulesets. Workflow YAML alone does not gate merges; the names have to be registered in branch protection for failures to actually block merging.

Closes #135
